profile.reading: Per QTS own site, RIC3 DC4 is located at 3539 Portugee Road, Sandston, VA 23150 on the QTS Richmond 3 campus, a 221 acre master-planned campus with 240 MW planned upon completion across five Freedom Design buildings (DC1-DC5). Individual building square footage and phased MW capacity are not published.

profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021, at $78/share. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
RIC3 DC4 sits on the QTS Richmond 3 campus, a 221 acre master-planned facility in Sandston that the operator describes as planned for 240 MW across five buildings upon completion. Individual building capacity is not published, so the contribution of this specific structure to that campus total cannot be determined from available data. The campus occupies a converted semiconductor manufacturing site, a pattern that shapes power and cooling infrastructure in this region.

At 240 MW campus total, assuming 8 kW per rack as a conservative estimate for mixed workloads, the Richmond 3 campus could host roughly 30,000 racks if fully populated for compute. If the split were weighted toward AI training at 40 kW per rack, the same power would support approximately 6,000 racks, though the actual configuration is not published. This campus ranks 24th among the 23 facilities with published megawatt figures in Virginia, placing it outside the state's disclosed capacity leaders but within a small set of tracked installations.

Virginia has mapped 326 data center facilities total, but only 23 have published power capacity. The state's disclosed total is 1,375 MW across those 23 sites, meaning Richmond 3's 240 MW planned capacity represents 17.5 percent of Virginia's tracked public figures. Whether this campus reaches its planned capacity, and when, will depend on grid availability and demand; neither timeline nor current operational status is published.
